implementation_state: Each request now has one RequestLifecycle that owns the single terminal transition. A stream distinguishes a clean end, an upstream error, a client disconnect, and an explicit cancellation; a disconnect is recorded as interrupted or cancelled and never as served. Every failure decision reads the canonical ClassifiedFailure impact table, and exactly one validated Outcome per request carries planned, last-attempted, and served identity. Accepted on dev at c4188be.
required_gates: Client drop/cancellation never recorded as success
unblock_condition: Accepted: identity correlation, one classified failure path, the buffered and streaming terminal lifecycle, the drop and cancellation terminal states, exactly-once Outcome construction, and single-site accounting are all proven by behavioral tests and the full dev gate set.
notes: This is the only Core repair node allowed to edit server/pipeline.rs; no concurrent pipeline worker is permitted.
It must not modify accepted ml/shadow.rs or model identity files, and it must not implement ML activation.
Implemented on branch node/core-p1-pipeline-lifecycle as cbe2240 and integrated into dev as c4188be; the parent review and gates are E-058 through E-061.

The REG-007 defect is closed: the drop path no longer finalizes a client disconnect as success. A client-closed request now shows activity status 499 and is counted as a failure, which is a deliberate user-visible change.
The pipeline fabricates no Feedback: it has no user-signal source, and ADR-0004 forbids inventing a rating. Exactly-once refers to the single Outcome, with zero Feedback.
The Outcome log is a bounded in-memory diagnostic ring. No DatasetStore, training, activation, or LearningEvent journal is wired, and the served identity is left available but unwired for 7E-1B.
